explanation: Track the largest and smallest one-value and two-value products while scanning. Each new value can extend either extreme two-value product to a three-value candidate.
correctness: Multiplication by a new negative value reverses order, so both extremes are sufficient. Updating three-value candidates before pairs and pairs before singles guarantees distinct positions.
walkthrough: For [-8,-5,2,4], the first two negatives have product 40. Combining that pair with 2 gives 80, and later with 4 gives 160. Selecting the three numerically largest values would miss this result; tracking both low and high pair products preserves the winning candidate.
edgeCases: For [-6,-3,-2,-1], return -6, even though it is negative. Equal values at different positions remain distinct eligible factors.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: one pass maintains a fixed set of extrema with constant work per value.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: the extrema and candidate product are scalars; the input is never sorted or copied.
